title: Minimum Operations to Equalize Array
summary: Given an integer array nums, determine the least number of operations needed to make all elements equal by replacing each element in a chosen subarray with the bitwise AND of all elements in that subarray.
statement: Given an integer array nums, determine the least number of operations needed to make all elements equal by replacing each element in a chosen subarray with the bitwise AND of all elements in that subarray.
constraints: One operation chooses a nonempty subarray and replaces every value in it by the bitwise AND of that entire subarray.
Return the minimum operations needed to make all array values equal.
Choosing the whole array is allowed.
hints: If all values already match, the answer is zero.
Otherwise at least one operation is necessary.
Choose the complete array; its AND is written to every position.
That one operation always equalizes a nonuniform array and is therefore optimal.
editorial: That one operation always equalizes a nonuniform array and is therefore optimal.

tests.explanation: The values differ, and one whole-array AND operation makes both zero.
All values already match, so zero operations are needed.
